# V139 reviewed Functions baseline

Current baseline: `79750515c9a523cf8b6a8d02ba1b4876793cf8f1`, the reviewed fitting-source retention release.
The additional Functions delta is limited to `jarvis-semantic-planner.js`.
Its existing audit packet keeps fitting source bodies inside the established
28,000-character ceiling after metadata compaction, instead of discarding them
at an earlier 16,000-character target. Runtime observation preserves bounded
raw source bytes and declares the actual retained line interval when clipped.
Replay of the real Chrome receipt retains all 18,139 characters and removes the
duplicate full-file action before inference. Complete empty query receipts may
reuse only their own successful template and resolved route; another literal
scope remains eligible. Neither rule credits operational objective completion.

All 321 focused planner/orchestrator checks pass on the clean functional HEAD.
The full local suite has 1,986 PASS, zero failures and one Linux-only skip,
including physical repository search against the live local bridge. Static
local-only policy, syntax and whitespace checks pass. Fresh CI, deployment
alignment and the full clean Chrome mission remain required. No model, provider
trigger, permissions or operational records change. The guard stays explicitly
pinned, ancestor-checked and fail-closed.

## Previous grounded evidence-history baseline

Previous baseline: `1c7b2788bc64c424bcec24de6c25fa09eddb18e9`, the reviewed grounded evidence-history release.
Only `functions/jarvis-semantic-planner.js` changes from the previous pin.
Argument completion now receives immutable objectives, original structured receipts
and tool evidence metadata before applying the same eligible-action filter used
by auditing. Fully retained reads and exact exhausted query scopes are removed
before inference; partial sources, new scopes and filters remain eligible.
An empty complete query without a count aggregate constrains only its own scope.
Pending goals without an accredited proof advance before independent negative
reviews; claims of completion, existing credited proof changes and final closure
still receive independent objective verification. No query exhaustion satisfies a goal.

The baseline reproduction permitted the duplicate full-file read; this revision
removes it before inference. All 270 evidence regressions pass on clean functional
HEAD. The full local suite has 1,984 PASS, zero failures and two explicit skips:
Linux-only browser transport and physical repository search while the workstation
is stopped for publication. Physical search must run after startup. Static local
policy and syntax checks pass. Real Chrome certification is still required.
No operational data, permissions, model or paid-provider triggers change.
The guard remains pinned to an explicit reviewed functional commit and fail-closed.

## Previous local evidence cycle baseline

Previous baseline: `42b8d627ecf76848e0a068018a110523fce1c75d`, the explicitly reviewed local evidence cycle release.
The additional Functions changes are limited to `jarvis-semantic-planner.js`
and `index.js`. The planner recognizes actual exhausted cursor receipts with

unfiltered reads before inference, and preserves other routes and filters.
Independent objective contracts, authenticated scopes, source prerequisites,
field credit and completion qualification remain mandatory. Code is never
operational evidence and exhausting a query never completes an objective.

Coverage is reviewed before selecting the next action. Engine-owned proof caches
are scoped to mission, actor, model, clarifications, source schemas and operational
dependencies; temporal contracts also depend on the evaluation instant. Only
independently checked source exclusions can omit unrelated record values, while
their query scope and observed field names still invalidate changed dependencies.
Reusing coverage preserves a valid action. Recovery permits one same-model
continuation, with the same schema, novelty and query relevance validation.

The three historical cloud research/media/image callables now fail closed before
provider invocation and no longer bind Gemini secrets. Their compatibility helper
unit tests remain simulated; they do not authorize or execute external inference.
Production startup pins Qwen3.5:9b, and model identity and per-stage timings are
observable. No alternate semantic authority or paid-provider trigger is added.

The full local suite passed 1,982 tests, zero failures and one Linux-only skip.
All 268 focused evidence regressions passed again on the clean functional HEAD.
The current static policy check explicitly does not claim physical certification.
Fresh CI, aligned deployed bytes and the complete clean Chrome mission remain
required. No operational records or permissions were modified. The guard remains
explicitly pinned, ancestor-checked and fail-closed.

## Initial workflow repair baseline

The initial workflow repair used `.github/scripts/v139-functions-guard.mjs` and the
explicit baseline `7f50f7d306f789a8dbde355435895b8d54abb872`. This is the integrated
branch HEAD before this workflow-only repair, not a dynamically accepted HEAD.
Platform CI run https://github.com/heberzzt-wq/fixgo-app/actions/runs/38281211531
passed at that exact SHA. This accepts already integrated Functions history;
it does **not** certify the canonical real reel or the unfinished local planner work.

## Why the previous base stopped working

The original August workflow isolated a frontend/bridge reel change from Functions
changes. Commit `36b13c88f74d5504384f203b58a928c896ea99db` explicitly rebased the
guard to an accepted head. Commit `78f2dd6e1984d1ccc392bae961d70238ad20484e`
advanced only Windows to `dbe0a94b660008d4620f9ce4726ca66b2a5db555`, a September 17
workflow commit restoring dispatch-only certification. It was a frozen accepted
branch snapshot, not a Functions dependency or immutable reel contract. Linux
subsequently retained `45c9231715ad1d8f50756328c6e4128deebba581` instead.
Both historical comparisons eventually rejected legitimate integrated evolution.
Run https://github.com/heberzzt-wq/fixgo-app/actions/runs/38101666190 failed at the
Windows guard and never ran the real mission or its marker.

Personnel, identity, crew, financial/service authorization and their tests belong
to integrated B2B/B2C functionality, not a new change introduced by this reel
certification. The generated platform contract follows that platform evolution.
Package additions include the biometric Human/TensorFlow/JPEG dependencies.
Secure entry and its aliases retire historical independent generator/withdrawal
authority and route callers to canonical security handlers.

The semantic planner and repository planner **are relevant to reel behavior**:
they must not be declared harmless merely because their changes are legitimate.
`index.js` and `jarvis-intent-runtime-v7.cjs` also retire cloud semantic authority
in favor of local-only Jarvis. The canonical script imports the semantic planner
directly and still constructs a Google/Vertex provider. Thus compatibility with
the current local-only policy, provider credentials, media generation and the
actual reel result remain subject to the real mission, not this guard.

The baseline deliberately includes this integrated history without reverting it.
It does not exempt any file from future review: **all** committed Functions
additions, removals, renames and modifications after the baseline still fail.
Any future legitimate Functions release needs an explicit reviewed baseline
advance with corresponding CI evidence; never substitute HEAD/event-before
automatically. A missing baseline, non-ancestor baseline, Git error, wrong branch,
or tracked/untracked Functions worktree change fails closed as well. Ignored
installed dependencies do not count as source changes.

## Certification and execution boundaries

The main workflow now runs `certify-v139` on push or manual dispatch, without
external credentials or a live provider call. All its existing syntax, focal,
business and full-CI checks remain; guard regressions are also run explicitly.
Its marker identifies local **compatibility tests only**, not an Ollama end-to-end
mission. This change neither installs nor selects another semantic model.

The former Windows job is retained in
`.github/workflows/v139-legacy-external-reel.yml`, with the same bridge/canonical
mission step and Windows certification marker. Its only trigger is manual
`workflow_dispatch`, gated by `authorize_paid_external_reel == true`; the boolean
input defaults to false and explicitly warns about Google/Vertex and Runpod usage
and potential charges. There is no push, schedule, workflow-call or downstream-run
trigger. No historical external mission is authorized or executed for this repair.
No marker executes following a guard or mission failure. Neither workflow suppresses
failures with `continue-on-error` or equivalent constructs.

An opt-in historical result is provider compatibility evidence, not certification
of the workstation's single Qwen3.5:9b/Ollama model. The current local mission and
unfinished planner work still require their separate real Chrome certification.
The other legacy canonical workflows are outside this repair; their push filters
do not match the files changed here and no workflow-run hook was found.
